Chancellor Huo Zali relayed the order to the Hanlin, and because Jufu was young, recommended him as Attendant Literary Official of the Hanlin. The emperor said, "From now on you are to tell me the rights and wrongs of state policy and which ministers are upright or corrupt."

Chancellor Horqosun relayed the order to the Hanlin, and because Jufu was young, recommended him as Attendant Literary Official of the Hanlin. The emperor said, "From now on you are to tell me the rights and wrongs of state policy and which ministers are upright or corrupt."
火禮霍孫 is the Mongol name Horqosun, not Huo Zali.
if Your Majesty asks about grain revenues, that is the Grand Herald's affair.
if Your Majesty asks about grain revenues, that is the Superintendent of Grain's affair.
治粟內史 is the Superintendent of Grain, not the Grand Herald.

In Taiding 2 he was posthumously made Grand Minister over the Masses and Pillar of the State, enfeoffed as Duke of Chu, with the posthumous title Wenxian.
大司徒 is the Grand Minister over the Masses, not the Grand Mentor.

Just then the Ministry of Revenue was being established, and Mengfu was ordered to draft the edict promulgated empire-wide. The emperor read it and said with delight, "This says exactly what I wished to say."

Just then the Department of State Affairs was being established, and Mengfu was ordered to draft the edict promulgated empire-wide. The emperor read it and said with delight, "This says exactly what I wished to say."
尚書省 is the Department of State Affairs, not the Ministry of Revenue.
If you don't cancel it now, later critics will blame the Ministry of Revenue for losing tens of millions in uncollected revenue—and won't that fall heavily on you as chief counselor?"
If you don't cancel it now, later critics will blame the Department of State Affairs for losing tens of millions in uncollected revenue—and won't that fall heavily on you as chief counselor?"
尚書省 is the Department of State Affairs, not the Ministry of Revenue.

Earlier Sangge had dispatched Xindu, Wang Ji, and others to audit land tax and grain levies empire-wide. Hundreds of millions had already been collected, yet tens of millions remained unpaid; the burden on the people was terrible—they could barely survive, suicides came one after another, and those fleeing to the hills were hunted by troops. No one dared stand in the way.

Earlier Sangge had dispatched Xindu, Wang Ji, and others to audit land tax and grain levies empire-wide. Several million had already been collected, yet tens of millions remained unpaid; the burden on the people was terrible—they could barely survive, suicides came one after another, and those fleeing to the hills were hunted by troops. No one dared stand in the way.
數百萬 means several million, not hundreds of millions.
Other high officials joined in, and the emperor had Sangge investigated and executed, abolished the Ministry of Revenue, and dismissed many ministers on charges of corruption.
Other high officials joined in, and the emperor had Sangge investigated and executed, abolished the Department of State Affairs, and dismissed many ministers on charges of corruption.
尚書省 is the Department of State Affairs, not the Ministry of Revenue.
Wei Qalghasun, commissioner of the surveillance commission, was notoriously cruel; resenting Mengfu's refusal to defer to him, he tried to incriminate him on a petty charge.
Wei Qalghasun, assistant commissioner of the surveillance commission, was notoriously cruel; resenting Mengfu's refusal to defer to him, he tried to incriminate him on a petty charge.
僉廉訪司事 is an assistant surveillance commissioner, not the commissioner.

In the fifth year he was appointed assistant commissioner of the Jiangnan and Zhexi Surveillance Commission. A Pingjiang monk who resented the prefectural judge Li Xi bribed his followers to accuse Xi of corruption, and Xi was forced to confess.
僉...肅政廉訪司事 is an assistant surveillance commissioner, not a concurrent one.

In the second year of Zhizhi he was summoned to serve as Direct Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies. An earthquake struck, and the throne ordered officials to discuss how calamities might be averted.
集賢直學士 is the Direct Academician, as rendered elsewhere in this chapter.

In the fifth year of Zhishun, by imperial decree Wenyuan was posthumously made Assistant Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, with the posthumous name Wensu.
參知政事 is rendered Assistant Administrator for consistency with this chapter.
After two performance reviews he was transferred to Drafting Academician.
After two performance reviews he was transferred to Drafting Attendant.
待制 is the Drafting Attendant, not an academician.

He was posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Court Audience, made Vice Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat and Defender of the Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Chenliu, and given the posthumous name Wenqing.

He was posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Court Audience, made Assistant Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat and Defender of the Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Chenliu, and given the posthumous name Wenqing.
參知政事 is rendered Assistant Administrator for consistency with this chapter.

Hanlin Recipient of Edicts Yan Fu rarely praised scholars from anywhere in the realm; when he met Yuanyong and showed him his own writings, Yuanyong at once pointed out their flaws. Fu was deeply impressed and recommended him as Compiler of the Hanlin National History Academy.
翰林承旨 is the Hanlin Recipient of Edicts, not a chancellor.
He was transferred to Director of the Right Branch of the Ministry of Revenue and then promoted to Vice Director.
He was transferred to Director of the Right Branch of the Department of State Affairs and then promoted to Vice Director.
尚書省 is the Department of State Affairs, not the Ministry of Revenue.

When the Department of State Affairs was abolished, he retired to Rencheng; in time he drew a great many students from Qi and Lu.
